messages:
Sam: quick q — runtime handshake for model admit. do we want the validator to call the runtime api directly for a full smoke, or have the runtime expose a tiny probe endpoint the validator hits?
Priya: probe endpoint + small signature makes sense. avoids heavy coupling and long cold-starts during admit.
Jordan: +1 on probe, but we should be careful about coupling semantics. if probe returns capability flags we still need a compatibility contract version.
Kai: what about a shared proto for the probe response? e.g. {version, kv_cache_supported, max_seq, quant_modes} so the admit pipeline can decide. keeps parsing stable.
Priya: yes — proto + stable enum for quant_modes. also makes private deploys easier (no runtime SDK).
Sam: ok. tradeoffs?
Jordan: tradeoff: probe reduces validation fidelity vs calling full runtime smoke which catches model-specific failures. probe might miss subtle runtime config issues.
Priya: true — propose two-phase: lightweight probe for quick gating (fast path) then schedule an async full-smoke bench run in the background (slow path) before marking model public. fast path keeps onboarding snappy.
Kai: agree. slow-path bench can run on a reserved queue and post back results. we need a clear failure taxonomy: probe-fail (block), smoke-fail (block until fixed), smoke-regression (warn + hold for manual review).
Sam: how should the validator authenticate to runtime probe? runtime could expose only on internal network for Dedicated/Hosted, but Private runs might need local adapter.
Jordan: require mTLS + service identity header. for Private, the private-admit agent will proxy probe calls and inject identity. avoids opening public endpoints.
Priya: also add a short TTL on probe responses to avoid using stale capability data. store capability fingerprint on model metadata.
bench-bot: bench job queued: model=redwood/open-3b-v2 commit=ab12cd status=pending queue=admit-slow-smoke
Kai: good. small implementation note: keep probe payload under 1KB and binary-stable. stick to fields we actually consume.
Sam: rollout plan? like, land proto + validator changes, then runtime probe support, then enable fast-path by default?
Priya: land proto + validator dry-run first (no block), collect metrics for 1 week, then flip fast-path to block if probe fails.
Jordan: also add a migration doc for older admitted models: how we reconcile missing capability fingerprint on them (treat as unknown, schedule slow-smoke).
Kai: long-term: consider moving the validator logic into a small sidecar that runs next to runtime in Private deploys. reduces network hop and keeps behavior consistent across modes.
Sam: that sidecar idea seems heavier but could simplify the adapter logic. add to backlog as b/infra-ml-210.
Priya: I'll draft the proto and an admit playbook (fast/slow semantics + telemetry + failure codes).
Sam: thanks — assign reviewers @Jordan @Kai.
Jordan: happy to review the proto. one more ask: include a small test harness (mock runtime probe) so unit tests can simulate capability combos.
Priya: will do, will attach example curl in the doc:
```
curl -sS --cert client.pem --key client.key https://runtime.internal/v1/probe | jq .
{
  "proto_version": "1",
  "model_fingerprint": "ab12cd",
  "kv_cache_supported": true,
  "max_sequence": 4096,
  "quant_modes": ["fp16", "int8-quant"]
}
```
Sam: perfect. creating RFC follow-up with those pieces. :thumbsup:
Priya: thanks — filing now.
summary: discussion about runtime probe vs full smoke, proto handshake, fast/slow admit path, auth and private deploy adapter, rollout plan
